problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Using Row Operations

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
examples.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine $A^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix $A^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".
